name: Lysanias
title: Tetrarch of Abilene
summary: Lysanias was the tetrarch (ruler of a fourth part) over the region of Abilene in Syria at the time when John the Baptist began his ministry. He is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Luke 3:1, as part of the historical dating for John's service. His mention serves as an important chronological anchor for dating the events of the Gospels.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as tetrarch of Abilene
keyEvents.description: Lysanias is mentioned as the tetrarch of Abilene in the detailed historical dating that Luke provides to mark the beginning of John the Baptist's ministry.

keyEvents.title: Historical context for John the Baptist's service
keyEvents.description: Luke places the appearance of John the Baptist in a precise historical framework by mentioning six political and religious leaders, including Lysanias, to anchor the gospel narrative in world history.

keyEvents.title: Part of the Roman Empire's governance structure
keyEvents.description: Lysanias' role as tetrarch of Abilene illustrates the complex political division in the eastern Mediterranean under Roman rule, where the region was split among several local rulers.

keyEvents.title: Witness to the coming of God's word
keyEvents.description: In the same historical context where Lysanias is mentioned, Luke tells us that the word of God came to John, son of Zechariah, in the wilderness – an event that marked the beginning of the messianic proclamation.
